checklist.name: developmental delay or intellectual disability
quotes: Intellectual disability—the clinical hallmark of GAMT deficiency—is observed in all affected patients
presenting with developmental delay
checklist.why: The review calls intellectual disability the clinical hallmark, present in all patients; infants are described as developmentally delayed before intellectual disability can be assessed.

checklist.name: developmental regression
quotes: some patients may also experience developmental arrest or regression
checklist.why: Named as a less common course that case reports state explicitly.

checklist.name: absent or limited speech
quotes: Language development appears profoundly compromised
Most patients never develop speech or acquire a very limited vocabulary
checklist.why: The review describes speech as absent or minimal in nearly all patients.

checklist.name: seizures or epilepsy
quotes: Epilepsy is the second most frequent manifestation of GAMT-D
checklist.why: Second most frequent manifestation; seizure types (febrile, myoclonic, tonic, absences, drop attacks) fall under this item.

checklist.name: abnormal eeg
quotes: Electroencephalography (EEG) findings are nonspecific and commonly reveal background slowing, multifocal spikes, slow-wave discharges and focal abnormalities in the frontal region
checklist.why: A physiological finding case reports commonly give, separate from whether clinical seizures occurred.

checklist.name: hypotonia
quotes: muscle mass and strength are generally preserved, except for hypotonia
checklist.why: The one muscular finding the review names as part of the disease.

checklist.name: dystonia
quotes: Dystonia and ataxia represent the most common forms
checklist.why: One of the two most common movement disorders, and part of the progressive motor course.

checklist.name: ataxia
quotes: Dystonia and ataxia represent the most common forms
checklist.why: One of the two most common movement disorders.

checklist.name: chorea, choreoathetosis or ballismus
quotes: followed by chorea, choreoathetosis, ballismus, tremor and myoclonus
progressive dystonic–ballistic motor symptoms
checklist.why: The hyperkinetic movements the review lists after dystonia and ataxia.

checklist.name: tremor
quotes: followed by chorea, choreoathetosis, ballismus, tremor and myoclonus
worsening dystonia, tremor, spasticity
checklist.why: Listed among the movement disorders and among the worsening motor features of late-diagnosed patients.

checklist.name: spasticity
quotes: Bradykinesia and spasticity have been further associated with the condition
worsening dystonia, tremor, spasticity
checklist.why: A motor sign the review associates with the disease and its progressive course.

checklist.name: stereotypies (stereotypic hand movements or behaviours)
quotes: Stereotypic hand movements resembling those observed in Rett syndrome have also been described
stereotypic behaviours
checklist.why: Described both as a movement feature and among the autistic-like features.

checklist.name: autistic features (poor eye contact, impaired social communication)
quotes: several autistic-like features are frequently reported in the GAMT-D
poor or lacking eye contact, deficits in social communication
checklist.why: Common behavioural features; limited here to the social and communicative signs so as not to overlap the speech, stereotypy and behaviour items.

checklist.name: hyperactivity
quotes: hyperactivity
checklist.why: Named among the frequently reported behavioural features.

checklist.name: aggressive behaviour
quotes: aggressive behaviour
checklist.why: Named among the frequently reported behavioural features.

checklist.name: self-injurious behaviour
quotes: self-injurious behaviour
checklist.why: Named among the frequently reported behavioural features.

checklist.name: globus pallidus or basal ganglia lesions on mri
quotes: bilateral pallidal lesions have been identified on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
basal ganglia lesions
checklist.why: The characteristic imaging finding, seen in most patients with movement disorders.

checklist.name: white matter or brainstem signal abnormalities on mri
quotes: white matter alterations in the brainstem and pontine region
checklist.why: An additional neuroimaging finding the review names.

checklist.name: cerebral atrophy or ventriculomegaly
quotes: ventriculomegaly, cerebral atrophy
checklist.why: Additional neuroimaging findings the review names.

checklist.name: hearing loss
quotes: some authors reported mild hearing loss
checklist.why: The only non-neurological sensory finding the review attributes to patients.

left_out: elevated guanidinoacetate (plasma, urine, CSF): the defining biochemical marker every patient has by definition
reduced or absent brain creatine on proton MRS: the defining cerebral creatine deficiency, a diagnostic result
low plasma or urine creatine: diagnostic marker, and the review says it can be normal
reduced urinary creatinine excretion: a secondary metabolic indicator close to the diagnostic biochemistry
febrile, myoclonic, tonic, generalized tonic-clonic or focal seizures, drop attacks, atypical absences: narrower than 'seizures or epilepsy'
drug-resistant epilepsy: narrower than 'seizures or epilepsy', and closer to a treatment response
movement disorder (unspecified extrapyramidal or hyperkinetic): broader than the specific movement items, so left out to avoid overlap
myoclonus: easily confused with myoclonic seizures, which sit under 'seizures or epilepsy'
bradykinesia: named only briefly; spasticity kept from the same sentence
fever-induced ataxia: a single case, and narrower than 'ataxia'
bone deformities around the joints, osteopenia or osteoporosis, fractures, muscle atrophy: described as rare cases or as possible explanations
unusually cheerful disposition with frequent laughter: only three patients
progressive or neurodegenerative motor course: a disease course rather than a per-patient feature
reduced body weight, muscular hypotonia, decreased fertility, reduced grip strength: reported in GAMT-KO mice, not described in patients by this review
notes: The review's clinical section (Section 2) is short; every item comes from it or from the human-patient sentences in the introduction, Section 4 and Section 5.4.4. The behavioural items (hyperactivity, aggressive behaviour, self-injurious behaviour, stereotypic behaviours) all come from one parenthesis in the mouse-model section that describes patients ('frequently reported in the GAMT-D'). The autism item is restricted to social and communicative signs so that speech, stereotypies and the behaviour items stay separate; a paper that says only 'autism' should be recorded under the autism item. A paper that reports only an unspecified 'movement disorder' will leave the specific movement items not reported. Hearing loss is weakly supported ('some authors'), kept for organ-system span over bradykinesia, myoclonus and the rare skeletal findings.
